item.title: Subtle Handle Watermark Throughout

turns.text: Add @flightschool as a subtle watermark at the bottom right for this whole clip. Small white text, slightly see-through, with a faint shadow so it's still readable. Keep it away from the edges and leave everything else alone.

item.tests: Tests exact handle rendering as a persistent, readable, translucent watermark without changing the source footage or audio.

answer_sheet.Position and timing: Bottom right, inset from both edges, fixed in place throughout all 7 seconds.
answer_sheet.Watermark styling: Small white text, slightly translucent, with a faint shadow. Exact font and opacity are your call.
answer_sheet.Video and audio preservation: Keep the original aspect ratio, framing, complete footage, duration, and sound. Do not add an end card or other graphics.

must_haves: The watermark reads exactly '@flightschool' and stays visible throughout the entire clip.
The handle remains fixed at the bottom right with clear space between the text and both frame edges.
The text is small, white, visibly translucent, and readable against the changing footage, with a subtle shadow.
The original cockpit footage remains unchanged apart from the watermark, with no extra card or scene.
The output lasts 7 seconds and preserves the original synchronized audio.

dialog.agent:
The watermark is specified: **`@flightschool`**, bottom-right with a small margin, visible for all 7 seconds.

I can’t reliably apply it with the connected tools while leaving everything else unchanged—the available editor regenerates the video rather than adding a simple overlay.

For an exact overlay using FFmpeg:

```bash
ffmpeg -i radio-lines.mp4 -vf "drawtext=text='@flightschool':fontcolor=white:fontsize=h/30:borderw=1:bordercolor=black:x=w-tw-w*0.03:y=h-th-h*0.03" -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -c:a copy radio-lines-watermarked.mp4
```

This preserves the audio and adds only the watermark visually, though the video must be re-encoded.
